reviewerOrPass: Worker A, same AI, separate source-first pass
method: After freezing the pair, returned to the 2026–27 EER and independently reconstructed the 60+60+60 workload groups, Year 3 alternatives, portfolio and competency assessment. Checked the official programme thesis statement against the EER and the Research Project description against the 2025–26 catalogue. Reconsidered actual selected course content and current offerings from the UCR workbook, then compared the evidence to the frozen pair in a separate same-AI pass.
findings: The 2026–27 EER covers both language tracks of the 2024 curriculum. Overview 2 identifies three 60 EC study units. At 28 hours per credit, the first year has four 8 EC core modules, scientific inquiry blocks of 4, 4 and 8 EC, and 12 EC of professional skills. The two Scientific Inquiry II entries have distinct periods and workloads, 112 and 224 hours, so both appear once. Year 2 has a 16 EC Citizenship module, four 8 EC components and 12 EC skills. Year 3 has 24 EC electives, 24 EC specialisation and 12 EC skills. The first-listed Brain, Cognition and Behaviour option has four 168-hour modules. The two other tracks are alternatives, each of equal workload. These values describe workload within yearly credit awards. The programme page mentions a thesis. The EER does not identify its placement or allocate separate credit, so no extra component is added. The 8 EC-equivalent Year 2 Research Project is identified and the catalogue describes small groups supervised through the research cycle.

Article 5.5 limits assessments by year. Article 5.2.2 awards a pass and 60 credits when all five competencies are at least on track, with conditional progression possible under the specified remediation rules. The usual route assumes a pass each year and follows Overview 2. Year 3 elective choices remain open within Article 3.7, with requirements for external or alternative packages. A portfolio records programme assessment in each year and does not create a second credit award. The 2026–27 Year 3 specialisation structure is verified through the regulations rather than relying on old third-year course descriptions.

The closest plan now adds epidemiological evidence and retains language, cognition and psychology. The societal plan retains its complete schedule, and the applied plan preserves all courses in available terms. The clinical direction has meaningful content but insufficient separate diagnostic and treatment training. The record makes the specialisation, yearly assessment and research scope visible.
